paper.title: LLM-Prop: predicting the properties of crystalline materials using large language models
paper.research_summary: This paper develops LLM-Prop, a method that leverages large language models (LLMs) to predict properties of crystalline materials from their text descriptions, outperforming state-of-the-art graph neural network (GNN)-based methods and domain-specific LLMs like MatBERT. It introduces the TextEdge benchmark dataset containing crystal text descriptions and their properties, and demonstrates that natural language input enables better capture of space group symmetry and Wyckoff sites than GNNs.

task.task_name_raw: predicting the properties of crystalline materials
task.objective: Predict physical and electronic properties of crystalline materials from their text descriptions
constraints: must use text descriptions as input
must outperform GNN-based methods and MatBERT
input_requirements: crystal text descriptions generated by Robocrystallographer
output_goal: numerical values for regression tasks (e.g., band gap in eV, volume in A³/cell) and classification labels (e.g., direct/indirect band gap)

evidence.text: LLM-Prop, a method that leverages the general-purpose learning capabilities of large language models (LLMs) to predict properties of crystals from their text descriptions.

stages.stage_name_raw: collecting dataset from Materials Project database
stages.stage_goal: Collect crystal structure-description pairs for training and evaluation

evidence.text: We collected the dataset used in this work from the Materials Project database40 using the Materials Project free API as of November 1, 2022.

stages.stage_name_raw: generating crystal text descriptions using Robocrystallographer
stages.stage_goal: Convert crystal structures into human-readable text descriptions

evidence.text: We generated the crystal text descriptions using Robocrystallographer41, a tool that generates a deterministic human readable text description of a structure given its CIF file.

stages.stage_goal: Prepare text descriptions for LLM input by removing stopwords, replacing numerical values with tokens, and adding [CLS] token

evidence.text: For the input preprocessing step we did the following: (1) We removed stopwords from the text descriptions... (2) We Replaced bond distance with a [NUM] token and bond angle with an [ANG] token... (3) We removed bond distances and bond angles... (4) We prepended a [CLS] token to the input.

stages.stage_name_raw: extracting property labels from Materials Project
stages.stage_goal: Obtain ground-truth property values for each crystal
stage_output: band gap, formation energy per atom, energy above hull, crystal volume, energy per atom, direct/indirect band gap indicator

evidence.text: We focus on six crystal properties that include both regression and classiﬁcation tasks and are diverse enough to evaluate the capabilities of any property predictor. We collect the data of band gap, formation energy per atom (FEPA), energy above hull (Ehull), crystal volume, energy per atom (EPA), and an indicator of whether the band gap is direct or indirect (Is-gap-direct).

stages.stage_name_raw: fine-tuning T5 encoder for property prediction
stages.stage_goal: Train LLM-Prop model on preprocessed text descriptions to predict crystal properties

evidence.text: Our LLM-Prop framework (Fig. 1a) is composed of a carefully ﬁne-tuned encoder part of small version of T5 model (Fig. 1b)31 on text descriptions of crystal structures to learn crystal representations that are used to predict the physical and electronic properties of any crystal material.

stages.stage_goal: Compare LLM-Prop's performance with GNN-based models and MatBERT on test set
stage_output: MAE for regression tasks, AUC for classification tasks

evidence.text: LLM-Prop outperforms the current state-of-the-art GNN-based methods by approximately 8% on predicting band gap, 3% on classifying whether the band gap is direct or indirect, and 65% on predicting unit cell volume, and yields comparable performance on predicting formation energy per atom, energy per atom, and energy above hull.
